msItem.title: Pontificale
msItem.note: 'Benedictionale et pontificale 2o fo Sancte Bartholomee' on vellum wrapper (now fol. iiv), written between double lines.

An alternative origin of Winchester has been proposed on the basis that it is a 'relatively straightforward copy of the Benedictional of St Æthelwold' (BnF, MS. lat. 987): A. Prescott, 'The Structure of English pre-Conquest Benedictionals', British Library Journal, sn (1987), 118-158 (quotation at 121).

provenance.orgName: Canterbury, Kent. Benedictine cathedral priory of Holy Trinity or Christ Church
provenance.p: 'Likely' origin of Christ Church, Canterbury briefly elucidated by N. R. Ker, 'A Supplement to Catalogue of Manuscripts Containing Anglo-Saxon', Anglo-Saxon England, 5 (1976), 121-31 at 127: notes that T. A. M. Bishop saw similarities in the script with the Arenberg Gospels (New York, Pierpont Morgan Library, MS M 869), and that the glossator translates 'thuribuli' as 'storcellan', using 'e' rather than West Saxon 'y'.

history.provenance: At fol. 1, 'Ex libris Hugonis Anderson, anno Christogonias Ducentesimo supra Sesquimillesimum'. The manuscript is now styled the 'Anderson Pontifical' after Hugh Anderson (d. 1749), minister of the parish of Drainie, Morayshire. From him to Robert Gordon: 'I leave this Book to Sr Robert Gordon his librarie witnes my hand at Kinneddar Octobris 6o an. Æ. C. 1741' (fol. 144).
Found in 1970 in the stables at Brodie Castle, in Forres, Scotland.
Put up for sale at Sotheby's, 12 July 1971, lot 35. Failed to reach reserve and bought in at £13,000. Sold to the British Museum.

recordHist.source: Neil R. Ker, ed., Medieval Libraries of Great Britain: A List of Surviving Books, Royal Historical Society Guides and Handbooks, 3 (London, 1941; 2nd edn, 1964; supplement, ed. Andrew G. Watson, 1987; digital edn, ed. Richard Sharpe and James M. W. Willoughby, 2010–15).
